layout_dets.text: Abstract

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Foundation segmentation models like Segment Anything (SAM) exhibit strong

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: generalization on natural images but struggle with localized failures in medical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: imaging, especially on fine-grained structures such as vessels with complex mor-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: phology and indistinct boundaries. To address this, we propose FineSAM++, a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structure-aware sparse expert framework designed to refine SAM outputs by in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: troducing a confidence-driven soft Routing Module. This module dynamically

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: identifies structurally uncertain regions and activates a lightweight Residual Expert

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to model and correct residual structural errors only within these areas, thereby

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: achieving efficient "refinement over retraining." Extensive experiments on five

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: public vascular segmentation datasets demonstrate that FineSAM++ consistently

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: outperforms both SAM-adapted baselines and task-specific models in terms of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: accuracy, topological consistency. Our results highlight the effectiveness of sparse,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structure-driven Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) strategies for enhancing the reliability

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of foundation vision models in clinical image understanding tasks.

layout_dets.text: 1 Introduction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Figure 1: Illustration of the core motivation behind FineSAM++.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Foundation vision models such as Segment Anything Model (SAM)[1] have demonstrated remarkable

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: prompt responsiveness and zero-shot generalization capabilities for natural image segmentation tasks.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: With the increasing popularity of SAM in general-purpose computer vision, recent efforts have

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: explored its adaptation to medical image segmentation [2–4]. However, empirical studies consistently

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: report substantial performance degradation when SAM is applied to medical structures, especially for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fine-grained targets like vessels, where predictions often suffer from topological errors, including

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: disconnections, boundary ambiguity, and local omissions [4, 5] (see Fig.1).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To bridge the domain gap between natural and medical images, existing approaches have explored

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: domain adaptation strategies including Adapters [6, 7], LoRA [8], prompt generation [9], and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SAM-CLIP hybrid models [10, 11] (see Fig.2). Nevertheless, these methods primarily focus on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: aligning global semantic representations, leaving structurally ambiguous or uncertain regions under-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: modeled [5, 4]. As a result, they fail to resolve the persistent issue of local structural degradation. We

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: further observe that mispredictions in medical images predominantly occur around blurred boundaries

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: or fine structural details, which typically manifest as high uncertainty or large residual deviations

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from the ground truth. This suggests that a unified global adaptation scheme inherently struggles to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: satisfy both semantic alignment and structural recovery, as the modeling objectives present a natural

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: conflict.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Figure 2: Comparison of SAM-based adaptation methods for medical image segmentation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Inspired by the sparse activation of Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures in large model design

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [12–14], we argue that MoE provides a promising paradigm for fine-grained structure modeling.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: By dynamically activating expert pathways only where necessary, an MoE-inspired framework can

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: focus modeling capacity on local difficult regions without sacrificing overall efficiency. Based on this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: principle, we propose FineSAM++, a structure-enhanced framework following the MoE philosophy.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: FineSAM++ introduces two expert modules: a global LoRA Expert for domain adaptation and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a Residual Expert for local residual correction and structural refinement. Their activation and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cooperation are jointly controlled by an uncertainty-aware Gating Module, resulting in an efficient

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shared-backbone + localized refinement strategy. Our main contributions are summarized as follows.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • We propose FineSAM++, the structure-aware sparse MoE framework that integrates multiple

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: localized residual correction pathways into frozen foundation segmentation models like

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SAM, addressing their systematic failures on fine-grained medical structures.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • We design a spatially-aware soft routing mechanism that jointly predicts spatial uncertainty

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: masks and fractional expert routing weights, dynamically activating only a small subset of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: residual experts for structurally ambiguous regions.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • We conduct extensive experiments to validate the effectiveness of the proposed module and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: achieve state-of-the-art performance on five public vessel datasets covering three distinct

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: imaging modalities.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2 Related Work

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2.1 Foundation Models for Medical Image Segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Foundation vision models such as the SAM [1] have demonstrated strong generalization and zero-shot

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: capabilities in natural image segmentation. However, their performance degrades significantly in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: medical imaging tasks, particularly for fine-grained structures like vessels and retinal layers, due

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to domain shifts and a lack of priors for thin, low-contrast anatomy[15, 16]. To bridge this gap

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: recent studies have explored adapter-based tuning [6, 7], LoRA-based silent fine-tuning [8], automatic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: prompt generation [9], and hybrid approaches combining SAM with CLIP [10, 11], as well as methods

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that improve boundary accuracy through high-quality priors and edge-aware refinement [17]. While

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: these methods improve global adaptability, they often overlook localized structural failures—such

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as vessel discontinuities, blurred edges, and fragmented predictions—that are critical in clinical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: applications [18]. FineSAM++ addresses this limitation by introducing a sparse residual expert

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: framework guided by uncertainty-aware gating, enabling selective correction of structurally uncertain

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: regions while preserving global semantic consistency.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2.2 Mixture-of-Experts Architectures in Vision Modeling

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures have emerged as a powerful paradigm for scaling deep

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: networks while maintaining efficiency [12, 13]. In vision, recent works have explored various

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: MoE formulations for different purposes. Switch Transformers [19] propose token-based routing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to conditionally activate expert blocks in large-scale transformers. Expert Choice Routing [14] and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SwitchHead [20] further improve routing efficiency and stability by optimizing expert selection and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: assignment. CuMo [21] introduces co-upcycled expert reuse to scale multimodal models, achieving

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: strong performance with limited expert redundancy. Neural Experts [22] and related vision-specific

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: MoE designs have focused primarily on large-scale classification and vision-language pretraining

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tasks. However, these works focus on token or patch-level routing for classification or vision-language

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tasks, and have not explored dense prediction or fine-grained structural correction. FineSAM++ to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: systematically integrate sparse expert routing into a dense segmentation pipeline. By introducing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a soft Gating Module and Residual Expert, FineSAM++ applies MoE principles to address local

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structural inconsistencies in medical vessel segmentation, which remains largely underexplored in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: prior vision MoE literature.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3 Method

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Inspired by the success of sparse MoE in scaling LLMs and vision models [12, 13], we propose

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: FineSAM++, a sparse expert framework designed for fine-grained targets. Fine-grained target

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation naturally fits the MoE paradigm due to the extreme sparsity, topology irregularity,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and strong locality of error-prone regions. Our framework incorporates two specialized lightweight

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: experts: a global LoRA Expert for domain adaptation and a Residual Expert for structure-aware

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: local residual correction. A differentiable Gating Module inspired by Expert Choice Routing [21]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: coordinates dynamic activation of experts.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4.1 Implementation Details

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Dataset. We evaluate FineSAM++ across five publicly available vascular segmentation datasets

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: spanning three imaging modalities. The DRIVE dataset [23] contains two-dimensional retinal fundus

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: images with ground truth vessel masks. ROSE [24] provides retinal vessel segmentation from 2D

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) scans. FIVES [25] includes 800 high-resolution

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: multi-disease color fundus photographs annotated for vessel structures. DCA1 [26] and CHUAC [27]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are coronary angiography datasets containing fluoroscopic X-ray vessel images. We select these

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: datasets to cover the full spectrum of challenges targeted by FineSAM++, including variations in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: anatomical regions (retina vs. coronary arteries), imaging modalities (fundus photography, OCTA,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: X-ray angiography), and segmentation difficulties (low contrast, thin structures, fragmented vessels).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Detailed dataset statistics and preprocessing steps are provided in the supplementary material.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Beyond vascular segmentation. To further assess cross-domain generalization, we additionally

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: evaluate multi-class abdominal organ segmentation on the Synapse Multi-Organ CT dataset (eight

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: organs), demonstrating that FineSAM++ maintains strong performance outside the vascular domain

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Detailed dataset statistics and results are provided in the supplementary material.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Training settings. All experiments are implemented using PyTorch and trained on two NVIDIA RTX

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4090 GPUs. Data augmentation includes random elastic deformation, rotation, scaling, and intensity

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: jittering. For the backbone, we follow [2] and integrate LoRA adapters into the frozen SAM encoder

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with a rank of 4. We adopt the ViT-B configuration of SAM as the base encoder. For fair comparison

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: across datasets, all images are resized to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resolution. The maximum training epoch is set to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 300. We use the AdamW optimizer with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: , and weight decay of 0.1. The initial

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: learning rate is set to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and decayed using a cosine annealing schedule. All hyperparameters

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Evaluation metrics. To comprehensively assess model performance, we evaluate FineSAM++ and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: all baselines across standard segmentation accuracy metrics and specialized structural consistency

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: metrics tailored for vascular image analysis. The primary evaluation metrics include Dice, accuracy

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (ACC), sensitivity (SE), specificity (SP), connectivity (C), overlapping area (A), vessel length

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: consistency (L), and centerline Dice (clDice). For completeness and reproducibility, detailed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: definitions for all metrics are provided in the supplementary material.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Compared methods. In this study, we comprehensively benchmark FineSAM++ against a wide

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: range of state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods previously reported on the evaluated datasets. The baselines

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: include both classical CNN-based and modern Transformer-based segmentation models, topology-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: aware segmentation method, as well as several recent SAM-variant foundation model adaptations.

layout_dets.text: Quantitative Comparisons. Tab. 1 summarizes the performance comparison across four datasets.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: FineSAM++ consistently achieves superior results over both CNN- and Transformer-based baselines

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as well as recent SAM-derived methods. On DRIVE and DCAI, FineSAM++ sets new state-of-the-art

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 0.7175) and H-SAM (0.6622 and 0.6374). On CHUAC and ROSE, our method also delivers the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: highest Dice scores (0.7768 and 0.8220), demonstrating robust generalization across diverse vascular

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: modalities. These results validate the effectiveness of our multi-expert sparse refinement strategy in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: addressing localized structural failures of foundation segmentation models while maintaining high

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: global consistency.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: leading SAM-variant methods (H-SAM, SAM Adapter, SAMed) across five datasets. Our method

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: consistently produces sharper and more continuous vessel structures with fewer false positives and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: disconnected branches. In coronary angiography datasets (CHUAC, DB134), FineSAM++ better

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: captures thin vessel bifurcations and suppresses background noise. On retinal fundus images (DRIVE,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: FIVES), our model recovers small peripheral vessels missed by baselines. For OCTA images (ROSE)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: FineSAM++ yields smoother centerlines with significantly reduced fragmentation compared to prior

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: approaches. These visual improvements highlight the advantage of our multi-expert sparse refinement

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: design for addressing localized structural errors while preserving global topology.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: across four datasets. FineSAM++ consistently achieves the highest CIDice scores, indicating superior

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: preservation of vessel topology and centerline continuity. On DRIVE and DCAI, our method

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: outperforms the strongest baseline by margins of 0.832 vs. 0.801 and 0.865 vs. 0.815 respectively.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: FineSAM++ not only improves segmentation accuracy but also enhances structural fidelity, which is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: critical in clinical vascular analysis.

layout_dets.text: Parameter Efficiency.To address concerns about the parameter efficiency of our proposed method

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: FineSAM++ among SAM-based segmentation approaches, we conducted a comprehensive compari-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: son under a standard input resolution of (1, 3, 1024, 1024). Specifically, we measured the number of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: parameters, FLOPs (GAMCs), and inference latency, as summarized in Table 3. As shown, Fine-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SAM++ introduces only about 0.7M additional learnable parameters over the SAM backbone (94.4M

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: efficiency. Moreover, while its total parameter count is higher than lightweight architectures like

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Unet, FineSAM++ achieves the highest Dice score (0.8231) among all evaluated methods. These

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: results indicate that FineSAM++ achieves an excellent balance between parameter efficiency and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation performance.

layout_dets.text: Ablation Study on the Gating Threshold δ. To assess the sensitivity of the Gating module

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SE, and SP. Intuitively, a too-small threshold treats most pixels as uncertain, triggering unnecessary

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: refinement and reducing gating sparsity, whereas a too-large threshold routes only a few pixels and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: 5 Conclusion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We presented FineSAM++, a structure-aware sparse expert framework for enhancing foundation seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation models in fine-grained medical image analysis. By introducing a soft Gating Module with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: uncertainty-aware spatial routing and deploying multiple Residual Experts with input perturbation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: diversity, our method achieves localized structural refinement while maintaining global consistency.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Extensive experiments on five vascular segmentation benchmarks demonstrate that FineSAM++

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: consistently outperforms both classical and SAM-adapted baselines across accuracy and topological

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: continuity. Our results validate the effectiveness of sparse expert activation for addressing localized

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation failures. Future work will explore dynamic expert allocation, adaptive perturbation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: strategies, and generalization to other medical and natural image dense prediction tasks.

layout_dets.text: A Dataset Details and Evaluation Metrics

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: A.1 Dataset Details

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We conduct experiments on five publicly available medical segmentation datasets. The 2D datasets

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: include DRIVE [23], ROSE [24], FIVES [25], DCA1 [26], and CHUAC [27].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: DRIVE [23]. The DRIVE dataset consists of 40 retinal fundus images (584 × 565 pixels) for vessel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation. We follow the official split of 20 training and 20 testing images.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ROSE [24]. The ROSE dataset contains 2D retinal optical coherence tomography angiography

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (OCTA) scans. We use the ROSE-1 (SVC) subset comprising 30 training and 9 testing images

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: FIVES [25]. The FIVES dataset (Fundus Image Vessel Segmentation) provides 800 high-resolution

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: color fundus images (2048 × 2048 pixels) with pixel-level vessel annotations. The dataset is split

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: into 600 training and 200 testing images.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: DCA1 [26]. The DCA1 dataset contains 134 coronary angiography images (300 × 300 pixels). We

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: follow the dataset's standard split with 100 training and 34 testing images.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: CHUAC [27]. The CHUAC dataset consists of 30 coronary angiography images (189 × 189 pixels)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with vessel annotations. Following [28], we split the dataset into 20 training and 10 testing images.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Synapse Dataset. The dataset [29] contains 30 subjects for training and 20 subjects for testing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with abdominal CT scans. It consists of 13 organs, including 8 organs of Synapse, along with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: esophagus, inferior vena cava, portal and splenic veins, right and left adrenal gland. Consistent with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the partitioning strategy outlined in [30].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: A.2 Compared Methods

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We compare FineSAM++ against a comprehensive set of state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods previously

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reported on the evaluated datasets. The competing approaches are categorized into three groups:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: CNN-based segmentation models, Transformer-based segmentation models, and foundation model

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: variants.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (1) CNN-based methods. Classical and recent CNN architectures include U-Net [31], Attention U-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Net [32], U-Net++ [33], CS-Net [34], VSSC Net [35], FR-UNet [36], ResU-Net [37], MedUNAS [38],

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: DUNet [39], HRNet [40], R2U-Net [41], GCN [42], Deeplab V3+ [43], CBAM [44], PSPNet [45],

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ENet [46], SK-Net [47], SegNet [48], COSFIRE [49], CE-Net [50], OCTA-Net [24], COOF [51],

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: MCDAU-Net [52], and MRC-Net [53].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (2) Transformer-based methods. Recent hybrid or fully Transformer architectures include Swin-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Unet [54], TransUNet [30], SGAT-Net [55], Retina-TransNet [56], CAViT [57], and G2ViT [58].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (3) SAM foundation model variants. To benchmark against foundation model-based baselines, we

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: include SAM Adapter [59], H-SAM [8], AutoSAM [60], SAMed [3].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (4) Topology-aware segmentation. the topology-aware adaptation by Gupta et al. [61].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: B Evaluation metrics

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To comprehensively assess the model's performance, we introduce the following evaluation metrics:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Dice coefficient (Dice), accuracy (ACC), sensitivity (SE), specificity (SP).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Dice. DICE score is a popular metric which measures the area/volumetric overlap between the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: predicted and ground truth discrete masks. It overcomes the class imbalance problem in the pixel-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: wise accuracy metric by considering only the foreground classes for measuring the overlap. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: higher the DICE, the better the segmentation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Accuracy (ACC). ACC measures the overall correctness of the segmentation results, calculating the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: proportion of correctly classified pixels or voxels to the total number of pixels or voxels.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Sensitivity (SE). SE also known as true positive rate or recall, quantifies the model's ability to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: correctly identify positive instances, indicating the proportion of true positives correctly classified

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: among all actual positives.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Specificity (SP). SP measures the model's ability to correctly identify negative instances, representing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the proportion of true negatives correctly classified among all actual negatives.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Connectivity (C). Connectivity evaluates the structural consistency between the predicted segmen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tation and the ground truth. It measures the extent to which the connectivity of predicted regions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: matches that of the ground truth, ensuring the preservation of continuous structures, particularly in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: medical images.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Overlapping Area (A). Overlapping Area measures the absolute area of intersection between the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: predicted segmentation and the ground truth. Unlike IOU, it focuses solely on the shared region size

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: often serving as a supplementary metric for segmentation overlap evaluation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Consistency of Vessel Length (L). L quantifies the similarity in vessel lengths between the pre-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dicted segmentation and the ground truth. This metric is particularly critical in vascular structure

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation, ensuring that the predicted vessels maintain accurate geometric proportions.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: clDice. A topology-based metric is particularly sensitive to a model's performance on thin structures.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: This metric evaluates the overlap between predicted and ground truth masks while incorporating the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: topological features of the segmentation output.

layout_dets.text: C.2 Generalization beyond vessel segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To validate that our framework generalizes beyond vessel segmentation, we evaluate multi-class

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: abdominal organ segmentation on the Synapse Multi-Organ CT dataset (eight organs). Following

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: prior work [30, 3, 8], we adopt the standard split of 18 training and 12 test volumes and apply the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: compared methods, surpassing strong baselines such as H-SAM and nnU-Net. Notably, our approach

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: maintains high accuracy on challenging small structures (e.g., pancreas), indicating that FineSAM++

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: preserves strong segmentation quality and robustness when extended to more delicate anatomical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: D Ablation study

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: D.1 Effect of Progressive Optimization with Dynamic Weighting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We evaluate the impact of progressive optimization with dynamic uncertainty-based loss weighting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by comparing three training strategies: (i) Naïve Joint Training, i.e., end-to-end optimization with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: uniform loss weights; (ii) Stage-wise (Independent), which freezes the coarse module and trains the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: refinement module separately; and (iii) Ours (Progressive), which progressively optimizes the two

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: modules with dynamic, uncertainty-aware weighting. As summarized in Table 9, the progressive

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: strategy consistently achieves the best overall performance across Dice, ACC, AUC, SE, and SP.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We attribute these gains to tighter interaction between the coarse and refinement modules and the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reweighting of supervision toward uncertain regions, which improves refinement quality without

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: overfitting.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Table 9: Ablation study on training strategies.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: D.2 Degrade Strategy for Robust Multi-Expert Refinement

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Refinement modules may overfit to thin structures, which can increase false positives or degrade

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mask quality in regions with weak boundaries or ambiguous textures. To mitigate this, we introduce

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a Degrade strategy in FineSAM++: rather than feeding all experts the same coarse mask, we

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: apply randomized degradations to the coarse mask (see Eq. (5)) to encourage input diversity and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: expert specialization. This promotes complementary expertise across residual experts and improves

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: robustness to structural uncertainty. As summarized in Table 10, enabling the Degrade strategy yields

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: consistent gains across Dice, ACC, AUC, and SP, while maintaining competitive SE, indicating fewer

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: false positives and stronger generalization.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Table 10: Ablation study of the Degrade strategy for multi-expert training.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: E Statistical significance.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We assess the statistical significance of our improvements using paired t-tests between our method

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and each baseline across all test images and datasets. Table 11 reports the resulting p-values for five

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: metrics (Dice, ACC, AUC, SE, SP); values in bold indicate

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: As shown, the majority of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: comparisons reach statistical significance, supporting that our approach yields superior segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: accuracy with improved consistency (lower variance) across datasets.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: F Societal impact discussion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: FineSAM++ is designed to mitigate localized failures in medical image segmentation—particularly in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fine-grained regions (e.g., vessels with blurred boundaries)—via a structure-aware, sparsely activated

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: expert mechanism that enhances fidelity with minimal computational overhead. This design advances

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: two practical goals: (i) improving the reliability of automated tools that support clinical decision-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: making, thereby reducing the risk of missed or spurious findings in delicate anatomical structures;

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and (ii) enabling a scalable, resource-efficient adaptation strategy that lowers deployment barriers in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: low-resource healthcare settings where retraining or maintaining large models is impractical.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: G Limitations

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: While FineSAM++ demonstrates strong performance and robustness across multiple vascular segmen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tation benchmarks, several limitations remain. First, the current design employs a fixed number of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Residual Experts with pre-defined perturbation settings, which may not fully capture the variability of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structural errors across highly diverse anatomical regions. Future work could explore dynamic expert

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: allocation or adaptive degradation strategies conditioned on image content. Second, FineSAM++

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: introduces additional complexity compared to single-expert or fully fine-tuned models. Third, our

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: study focuses primarily on vascular datasets. Extension to other fine-grained medical segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tasks, such as tumor boundary refinement or organ delineation, remains to be validated. We believe

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: these directions provide promising opportunities for further improving the generality and applicability

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of sparse expert refinement frameworks.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The assumptions made should be given (e.g., Normally distributed errors).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • It should be clear whether the error bar is the standard deviation or the standard error

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the mean.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • It is OK to report 1-sigma error bars, but one should state it. The authors should

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: preferably report a 2-sigma error bar than state that they have a 96% CI, if the hypothesis

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of Normality of errors is not verified.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • For asymmetric distributions, the authors should be careful not to show in tables or

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: figures symmetric error bars that would yield results that are out of range (e.g. negative

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: error rates).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • If error bars are reported in tables or plots, The authors should explain in the text how

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: they were calculated and reference the corresponding figures or tables in the text.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 8. Experiments compute resources

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Question: For each experiment, does the paper provide sufficient information on the com-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: puter resources (type of compute workers, memory, time of execution) needed to reproduce

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the experiments?

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Answer: [Yes]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Justification: For experiments, the paper provides information on the computer resources

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: needed to reproduce the experiments.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Guidelines:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The answer NA means that the paper does not include experiments.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The paper should indicate the type of compute workers CPU or GPU, internal cluster,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: or cloud provider, including relevant memory and storage.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The paper should provide the amount of compute required for each of the individual

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: experimental runs as well as estimate the total compute.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The paper should disclose whether the full research project required more compute

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: than the experiments reported in the paper (e.g., preliminary or failed experiments that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: didn't make it into the paper).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 9. Code of ethics

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Question: Does the research conducted in the paper conform, in every respect, with the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: NeurIPS Code of Ethics https://neurips.cc/public/EthicsGuidelines?

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Answer: [Yes]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Justification: The research conducted in this paper complies in all respects with the NeurIPS

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Code of Ethics.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Guidelines:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The answer NA means that the authors have not reviewed the NeurIPS Code of Ethics.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • If the authors answer No, they should explain the special circumstances that require a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: deviation from the Code of Ethics.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The authors should make sure to preserve anonymity (e.g., if there is a special consid-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: eration due to laws or regulations in their jurisdiction).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 10. Broader impacts

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Question: Does the paper discuss both potential positive societal impacts and negative

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: societal impacts of the work performed?

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Answer: [Yes]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Justification: The paper discusses the possible social impact of the work carried out.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Guidelines:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The answer NA means that there is no societal impact of the work performed.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • If the authors answer NA or No, they should explain why their work has no societal

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: impact or why the paper does not address societal impact.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • Examples of negative societal impacts include potential malicious or unintended uses

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (e.g., disinformation, generating fake profiles, surveillance), fairness considerations

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (e.g., deployment of technologies that could make decisions that unfairly impact specific

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: groups), privacy considerations, and security considerations.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The conference expects that many papers will be foundational research and not tied

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to particular applications, let alone deployments. However, if there is a direct path to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: any negative applications, the authors should point it out. For example, it is legitimate

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to point out that an improvement in the quality of generative models could be used to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: generate deepfakes for disinformation. On the other hand, it is not needed to point out

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that a generic algorithm for optimizing neural networks could enable people to train

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: models that generate Deepfakes faster.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The authors should consider possible harms that could arise when the technology is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: being used as intended and functioning correctly, harms that could arise when the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: technology is being used as intended but gives incorrect results, and harms following

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from (intentional or unintentional) misuse of the technology.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • If there are negative societal impacts, the authors could also discuss possible mitigation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: strategies (e.g., gated release of models, providing defenses in addition to attacks,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mechanisms for monitoring misuse, mechanisms to monitor how a system learns from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: feedback over time, improving the efficiency and accessibility of ML).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 11. Safeguards

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Question: Does the paper describe safeguards that have been put in place for responsible

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: release of data or models that have a high risk for misuse (e.g., pretrained language models,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image generators, or scraped datasets)?

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Answer: [No]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Justification: The paper uses public datasets.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Guidelines:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The answer NA means that the paper poses no such risks.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • Released models that have a high risk for misuse or dual-use should be released with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: necessary safeguards to allow for controlled use of the model, for example by requiring

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that users adhere to usage guidelines or restrictions to access the model or implementing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: safety filters.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • Datasets that have been scraped from the Internet could pose safety risks. The authors

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: should describe how they avoided releasing unsafe images.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • We recognize that providing effective safeguards is challenging, and many papers do

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: not require this, but we encourage authors to take this into account and make a best

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: faith effort.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 12. Licenses for existing assets

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Question: Are the creators or original owners of assets (e.g., code, data, models), used in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the paper, properly credited and are the license and terms of use explicitly mentioned and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: properly respected?

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Answer: [Yes]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Justification: The creators or original owners of assets used in the paper (e.g., code, data,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: models) are appropriately acknowledged, and the licenses and terms of use are clearly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentioned and appropriately respected.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Guidelines:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The answer NA means that the paper does not use existing assets.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The authors should cite the original paper that produced the code package or dataset.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The authors should state which version of the asset is used and, if possible, include a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: URL.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The name of the license (e.g., CC-BY 4.0) should be included for each asset.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • For scraped data from a particular source (e.g., website), the copyright and terms of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: service of that source should be provided.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • If assets are released, the license, copyright information, and terms of use in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: package should be provided. For popular datasets, paperswithcode. com/datasets

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: has curated licenses for some datasets. Their licensing guide can help determine the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: license of a dataset.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • For existing datasets that are re-packaged, both the original license and the license of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the derived asset (if it has changed) should be provided.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • If this information is not available online, the authors are encouraged to reach out to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the asset's creators.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 13. New assets

layout_dets.text: Question: Are new assets introduced in the paper well documented and is the documentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: Guidelines:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The answer NA means that the paper does not release new assets.

layout_dets.text: • Researchers should communicate the details of the dataset/code/model as part of their

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: submissions via structured templates. This includes details about training, license,

layout_dets.text: limitations, etc.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The paper should discuss whether and how consent was obtained from people whose

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: asset is used.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • At submission time, remember to anonymize your assets (if applicable). You can either

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: create an anonymized URL or include an anonymized zip file.

layout_dets.text: 14. Crowdsourcing and research with human subjects
